# Qwen3.8-27B — nvfp4 4-bit (shift + block scale + GPTQ) for the Farabi engine

A 4-bit `nvfp4` (group size 16) quantization of [Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) for Apple Silicon (MLX),
about 17 GB. Text and image input.

**This repository is meant for the [Farabi engine](https://github.com/maximianuu/farabi).** `config.json` carries a compensation
value (`farabi_lm_head_shift`) that the engine applies when loading. Other MLX loaders will read the tensors but will not apply it, and
their output distribution will be wrong.

## What was changed (Apache 2.0, section 4b)

Starting from the original bf16 weights:

1. Linear weights are quantized to 4-bit `nvfp4`. The token embedding table and the gate projections of the linear-attention layers
   (`in_proj_a`, `in_proj_b`) are kept in bf16.
2. Each matrix is multiplied by a power of two before quantization so that its per-block scales stay in the normal range of the 8-bit
   scale format; the inverse factor is folded exactly into the neighbouring norm weights (or `in_proj_a` / `in_proj_b`), and for
   `lm_head` it is stored in `config.json`. Block scales are fitted by least squares instead of max-abs.
3. Rounding is error-compensated layer by layer (GPTQ) on about 58k tokens of calibration text.

No fine-tuning: the model's behaviour is intended to match the original as closely as 4 bits allow. The tokenizer, chat template and
preprocessor files are unchanged.

## Fidelity

Against the original bf16 model, 8,087 token positions (KL divergence / top-token agreement): **0.085 / 93.5%**. The stock MLX `nvfp4`
conversion of the same model measured 0.339 / 82.4% in the same test. One machine, one test set; see `compression-report.json` for
per-module quantization error.

## Calibration data

Thinking chats generated by the model itself, question/answer chats, one chat behind a long system prompt, technical prose in Turkish
and English, Python and Swift source code, a tool-calling chat and JSON answers. The exact set is private; the public recipe is in the
engine repository (`tools/calibration.py`). The calibration text only steers rounding decisions; it is not stored in the weights.

## Use

```bash
hf download maximianuu/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4-gptq --local-dir ~/.farabi/models/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4-gptq
hf download maximianuu/qwen3.8-27b-mtp --local-dir ~/.farabi/models/qwen3.8-27b-mtp      # draft head, needed for speculative decoding
python -m engine.server
```

Apache 2.0, same as the original model. "Qwen" is a name of its owner; this is an unofficial conversion.
